title: Zephyrine and the Witness
premise: Dominic Kavanagh, a night dispatcher who quietly solves her clients' problems off the books, is paid an enormous retainer by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder scheduled for the spring tide will never happen. The intended victim, it turns out, is already legally dead — drowned eleven years ago in a case the police closed without ever recovering a body. As Dominic digs into the old verdict, she finds the 'victim' living under a new name and the original investigators tangled in something far dirtier than negligence. To stop the coming murder, she must prove the old one never happened at all — and when the tide finally gives up what it took, the evidence points at the man who hired her: the corrupt former detective who faked the drowning, now trying to silence his last witness before a grand jury convenes.
about_author: Ulyana Sandoval spent six years answering phones for a coastal cab company before turning the voices in her headset into fiction. She writes mysteries about people whose jobs begin where the law's paperwork ends.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A cash-heavy client named Aldous Wren hires her to prevent a murder he says will happen at the next spring tide, refusing to name the victim. Dominic takes the case out of pride and curiosity. Emotional beat: the thrill of an impossible commission shadowed by the first flicker of unease.

chapters.title: The Closed File
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Her only lead on the victim is a name from Wren's slip of tongue: Mara Voss — who drowned in 2013, case closed, no body recovered. Dominic pulls the file and finds sloppy work, a rushed coroner, and a detective named Halloran who pushed the closure through. Beat: cold dread beneath professional focus.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Isn't Dead
chapters.summary: Alternating Dominic and Mara POV. Dominic tracks a woman matching Mara's description working at a marina bait shop; Mara senses someone asking questions and prepares to run again. They meet, wary, each testing the other. Beat: two guarded women recognizing they need each other but can't yet trust.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flashback chapter: how Mara witnessed Halloran take bribes from a smuggling ring, how he staged her drowning to bury her testimony, and how she has lived ghost-like for eleven years. Beat: grief and rage; the reader learns the murder Wren fears is Mara's second death.

chapters.title: The Client's Confession
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic confronts Wren, who admits he was Halloran's partner and is dying; he wants his last act to be protecting Mara from Halloran's cleanup crew. He gives her a ledger as insurance. Beat: moral vertigo — her client is both guilty man and penitent.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Halloran's men make Dominic, torching her taxi office as a warning. She loses her dispatch board, her records, nearly her life. Beat: fear hardening into fury; the cost of the case becomes personal.

chapters.title: Grand Jury, Ghost Witness
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A young prosecutor reopens the Voss case after anonymous documents arrive (Wren's doing), and Mara must decide whether to surface from hiding and testify. Beat: terror versus the longing to exist again under her own name.

chapters.title: The Long Night Shift
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Using her dispatcher network — cabbies, harbor workers, night owls — Dominic maps Halloran's crew and discovers their plan to kill Mara before she reaches the courthouse at dawn. Beat: quiet competence assembling into a counter-plan; found-family warmth.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Climax at the marina pre-dawn: Halloran corners Mara on the pier where she 'died'; Dominic arrives with cabbies blocking every exit and Wren's ledger forcing the prosecutor's arrest team in behind them. Halloran, exposed, tries to finish the job and is taken by the tide's edge and the law together. Beat: breathless, then release.

chapters.title: Closed, For Good
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, weeks later. The old case is officially reopened and rightly closed; Mara testifies under her own name and gets her identity back. Wren dies with his debt partly paid. Dominic takes a new client, but keeps Mara's number pinned above her desk. Beat: earned peace, justice outside the law folded back into it.
